newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel slams call for Arab states to review ties.
newsitem.headline: Israel slams call for Arab states to review ties.

text.p: Israel on Saturday slammed a call by a committee headed by King Hassan of Morocco urging Arab and Moslem states to reconsider ties with Israel over its building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"Israel views the decisions of the Jerusalem Committee taken in Rabat and generally the call to Arab states to reconsider relations with Israel as harming the peace process and as another obstacle in its way," a Foreign Ministry statement said.
"Normalisation has to be an integral part of the peace process and this path cannot be forsaken and substituted with actions of a dictatorial and threatening style."
It demanded foreign ministers of countries belonging to the Arab League who are to meet in Cairo on Sunday take action to restore calm to the region.

"Israel expects from responsible regional leaders, foreign ministers of the Arab League convening in Cairo tomorrow, to call for an immediate end of terrorism, to stop the rhetorical deterioration, and to contribute to the real furtherance of understanding between the sides in the framework of direct negotiations."
Morocco's official news agency MAP reported on Saturday that the Jerusalem Committee, which ended a meeting in Rabat on Thursday night, had said in a final statement:

"The committee exhorts Islamic states which took steps towards establishing relations with Tel Aviv in the framework of the peace process, to revise their ties with Israel including the closure of missions and offices."
It said its recommendation would stay in effect until Israel respected United Nations resolutions related to the peace process and commitments made at Oslo and Madrid.
It called on Israel to halt the settlement building in Arab East Jerusalem.
Israeli troops on Saturday shot dead a Palestinian during clashes in the West Bank, causing the first fatality in 10 consecutive days of unrest sparked by the settlement building.
